passages.text: Peter said, “So that I do not spend time in a more contentious debate, rightly demanding that you answer my questions, I will give the answers as you wish, although I was the one who asked. I say that the one who provides is good, as I see the maker himself doing when he provides the sun to good and evil people and rain to the righteous and unrighteous.” Simon said, “This is most unjust: he provides the same things to the righteous and unrighteous.” Peter said, “Then you tell us from now on how he would act to be good.” Simon said, “You must say.” Peter said, “I will. If, by providing the same things to the good and righteous and also to the evil and unrighteous, he is according to you not even just, and if, by providing good things to the good and bad things to the bad, you would reasonably call him just, what further course of action could he take, if not this way: providing temporary things to the evil, in case they change, and eternal things to the good, provided they remain? Thus, in providing for all but granting favors to different recipients, his justice is good and all the more patient in this respect, if he forgives the sins of sinners who repent and also promises eternal life to those who have acted well. But in judging at the end and assigning to each what is deserved, he is just. If, then, these matters rightly stand this way, acknowledge it; but if they do not seem right to you, refute them.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐγώ φημι ἀγαθὸν εἶναι τὸν παρεκτικόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: I say that the one who provides is good
lexical_decisions.rationale: The articular τὸν παρεκτικόν is the accusative subject of εἶναι; ἀγαθόν predicates goodness of that provider. The English retains that direction rather than defining “the good person” as the provider. “Generous” is a contextual alternative for παρεκτικός, but the main text keeps providing explicit, as illustrated by the maker’s provision of sun and rain in the rest of the sentence.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἁμαρτωλοῖς μὲν μετανοοῦσιν χαρίζεται τὰ ἁμαρτήματα
lexical_decisions.chosen: he forgives the sins of sinners who repent
lexical_decisions.rationale: The complete μετανοοῦσιν denotes the sinners’ moral-spiritual response in this forgiveness context. “Who repent” follows the October 13 contextual policy, superseding the former mandatory reorientation gloss. It expresses a changed disposition toward wrongdoing, not merely sadness or a new opinion, without requiring proof of already completed reform or supplying an unprinted Godward phrase. The participle is distinct from the encompassing if, which remains separately retained for printed εἰ; forgiveness is not removed or made unconditional.
ὑπογράφω can pledge, prescribe, or outline. Promises fits the positive undertaking to those who act well, without claiming automatic possession already.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς σοὶ δοκεῖ αὐτὸς ὢν ἐπυθόμην ποιήσομαι τὰς· ἀποκρίσεις.
lexical_decisions.chosen: I will give the answers as you wish, although I was the one who asked.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied construction juxtaposes participial ὢν with finite ἐπυθόμην irregularly. The English reads this contextually as Peter answering despite having himself asked. A relative ὃς in place of printed ὢν would support a smoother clause but would be conjectural; it is not substituted. The supplied stop between article and noun in τὰς· ἀποκρίσεις is a print punctuation feature, not an alleged OCR defect.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ μὲν πᾶσιν παρέχειν, διαφόροις δὲ χαρίζεσθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: in providing for all but granting favors to different recipients
lexical_decisions.rationale: διαφόροις is taken as a dative of recipients, contrasting everyone with differentiated beneficiaries. It can also mean distinguished or worthy recipients; the main text leaves the difference unspecified. The previous different-gifts rendering would require an instrumental interpretation, by differing gifts, rather than an accusative object; that is a material alternative but the recipient reading is more direct with χαρίζεσθαι.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ μακρόθυμον ταύτη μᾶλλον, εἰ ἁμαρτωλοῖς μὲν μετανοοῦσιν χαρίζεται τὰ ἁμαρτήματα, εὖ πράξασιν δὲ καὶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον ὑπογράφει.
lexical_decisions.chosen: and all the more patient in this respect, if he forgives the sins of sinners who repent and also promises eternal life to those who have acted well.
lexical_decisions.rationale: If preserves εἰ governing the argument through both forgiveness and the promise of life. The participle “who repent” is distinct from that condition; the sentence is not changed into an unconditional assertion by a colon. The contextual repentance gloss does not change the participants or the relation among response, forgiveness, and eternal life.

μεταβάλλω is a distinct change expression, not μετανοέω. The moral context permits a change of conduct, but the existing “change” is retained instead of homogenizing this distinct verb into “repent” or adding a Godward formula.
